messages.content:
Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000610" [constraint]: The ledger service deploys on Wednesdays between 09:00 and 11:00 UTC.  (about: ledger service)
- memory_id "1000628": The Cinder team observed that the auth gateway's cold start time tripled after the runtime upgrade.  (about: Cinder team, auth gateway, the runtime upgrade)
- memory_id "1000650": On 2025-09-16, the Ember team handed the authentication gateway over to the Cinder team.  (about: Cinder team, Ember team, authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000575": INC-2025-017 was an incident where the auth gateway rejected every login for 12 minutes on 2025-08-02.  (about: auth gateway, INC-2025-017)
- memory_id "1000748": As of 2025-10-16, the Cinder team sits on the third floor.  (about: Cinder team)
- memory_id "1000727": As of 2025-10-13, the ledger service is owned by the Cinder team.  (about: Cinder team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000723": From 2025-10-13, the pager for the ledger service rings the Cinder team instead of the Atlas team.  (about: Atlas team, Cinder team, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000195" [constraint]: The billing API only ships on weekdays after 15:00 UTC.  (about: billing API)
- memory_id "1000664": As of 2025-09-23, the pager for the job scheduler rings the Cinder team.  (about: Cinder team, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000823" [decision]: As of 2025-11-27, Yuki Tanaka is on call for the Cinder team this cycle, taking over from Diego.  (about: Yuki Tanaka, Cinder team, Diego)
- memory_id "1000667": As of 2025-09-23, the Cinder team owns the job scheduler; team Dune owned it until then.  (about: Cinder team, team Dune, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000660": As of 2025-09-23, the Cinder team owns the job scheduler, which team Dune owned until then.  (about: Cinder team, team Dune, job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000248": The ledger service depends on the auth gateway for service tokens.  (about: ledger service, auth gateway)
- memory_id "1000881" [decision]: As of 2025-12-19, the Atlas team owns the product catalog, which the Cinder team owned until then.  (about: Atlas team, Cinder team, product catalog)
- memory_id "1000395": The Cinder team observed that the webhook dispatcher's memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change.  (about: Cinder team, webhook dispatcher, the cache change)
- memory_id "1000212" [constraint]: Per the change policy, the authentication gateway deploys on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC.  (about: authentication gateway)
- memory_id "1000430": INC-2025-011 was a ledger service incident on 2025-05-24.  (about: ledger service, INC-2025-011)
- memory_id "1000312" [constraint]: Per the change policy, the webhook dispatcher deploys on Mondays and Wednesdays between 14:00 and 16:00 UTC.  (about: webhook dispatcher)
- memory_id "1000599" [constraint]: As of 2025-08-19, deploys to the job scheduler happen only on Tuesdays and Fridays between 09:00 and 10:30 UTC; the old Tuesday 13:00-15:00 UTC window is retired.  (about: job scheduler)
- memory_id "1000279" [constraint]: The reporting service only ships on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC.  (about: reporting service)
Existing entity names: ledger service, Cinder team, auth gateway, the runtime upgrade, Ember team, authentication gateway, INC-2025-017, Atlas team, billing API, job scheduler, Yuki Tanaka, Diego, team Dune, product catalog, webhook dispatcher, the cache change, INC-2025-011, reporting service

The note says "auth-gateway deploys only on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC" which matches the authentication gateway deployment window (Mondays 10:00-12:00 UTC).

The note could be treated as confirming existing constraint 1000212, requiring no change. Per instructions: "If the note contains nothing durable, return an object whose arrays are empty." A reminder that restates an existing constraint is not new durable information. However, the alias "auth-gateway" → "authentication gateway" could be worth adding? The alias mechanism: "A name the note uses for an entity that already exists under another name." The note uses "auth-gateway"; existing entity is "authentication gateway". That seems legit to add an alias. But wait, "auth gateway" also exists as a name — is "auth-gateway" an alias for "auth gateway" or "authentication gateway"? The deployment window matches "authentication gateway" (memory 1000212). But many facts treat "auth gateway" and "authentication gateway" as the same thing (INC-2025-017 is about auth gateway rejecting logins; 1000248 ledger depends on auth gateway for service tokens; the handover was of authentication gateway to Cinder team). Likely same entity, but the memory system lists them as separate names.

Safest: the note adds nothing new durable; it's a reminder. But the alias mapping could be useful. Given the note's name "auth-gateway" with hyphen, and existing names "auth gateway" and "authentication gateway" both present, which canonical? The deployment window constraint (1000212) is about "authentication gateway". So map "auth-gateway" → "authentication gateway"? Or → "auth gateway"? Hmm.

Actually, the simplest reading: the note restates an existing constraint. No new facts needed. Possibly add alias for "auth-gateway". I think adding the alias is appropriate per instructions: "When the note uses a different name for an existing entity, add an entity_aliases entry mapping the note's name to the existing name."

Which canonical name? The constraint memory 1000212 uses "authentication gateway" and has the same deploy window. I'll map "auth-gateway" to "authentication gateway".

Alternatively, one might treat the note as reinforcing with "only" — a slight strengthening. The existing fact says "deploys on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC" (per change policy). The note says "deploys only on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC". The "only" could be considered a correction to make it exclusive. I think a correction to 1000212 adding "only" could be justified. But over-eagerness risk: the reminder is just restating. Hmm.

The guidance says "Do not invent anything the note does not say." The note does say "only". The existing fact lacks "only". Updating the constraint to include "only" is faithful. I could add a correction with old_memory_id "1000212", new_content "Per the change policy, the authentication gateway deploys only on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC." with evidence "auth-gateway deploys only on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC."

But is that a change or a redundant confirmation? The old text already implies Monday-only via "Per the change policy" presumably, but the text doesn't say "only". A reminder that says "only" strengthens it. I think a correction is reasonable but arguably unnecessary. Given memory systems benefit from precise constraints, I'll include the correction.

Hmm, but the risk: duplicates. If I add a new fact "The auth gateway deploys only on Mondays between 10:00 and 12:00 UTC", that duplicates 1000212. Better to correct 1000212 to include "only".

Decision: output correction with old_memory_id "1000212", new content including "only", entity "authentication gateway", kind "constraint", evidence quote.

Also add entity alias "auth-gateway" → "authentication gateway".

No new relations.

The developer schema says "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". The generic system message says to use ``` to end code block. Hmm. The developer instruction is more specific and authoritative: "one JSON object and nothing else, no prose, no code fence". The system message says always output valid JSON and use ``` to end code block. Conflict: developer says no code fence. I'll follow the developer: raw JSON, no fence.
